intro: Wide intervals can cover everything while providing little information. Report empirical coverage together with width to make the tradeoff visible.
task: Audit interval inclusion and width together so that broad intervals cannot hide behind coverage alone.
requirements: targets, lower, and upper are equal-length nonempty finite numeric vectors. Every lower endpoint must be at most its upper endpoint.
Return dict covered as a boolean vector using inclusive bounds, coverage as its mean, widths as upper-lower, and mean_width as the mean width.
Count boundary observations as covered. Zero-width intervals are valid and cover only exact equality. These are descriptive evaluation statistics.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Separate each row from the aggregate
hints.body: Build a boolean inclusion mask and a width vector before averaging.

hints.title: Use inclusive comparisons
hints.body: Equality with either endpoint counts as covered.

explanation: Empirical coverage is the fraction of evaluated targets inside their intervals. Mean width supplies the second dimension needed to distinguish informative coverage from trivially broad intervals.
These observations do not guarantee future coverage. Dataset shift and small evaluation samples can make a seemingly well-calibrated model unreliable.
